notes:
Background: Large claims processing platform used by regional carriers. 2025 roadmap: automate first-pass claim triage + real-time chat for adjusters. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and strict latency SLOs.

POC summary: ran 10-day perf POC (jan 22–feb 1). Workload: mixed chat + document embedding + reranking. Avg request shape: 1.2k tokens for extraction calls, 600 tokens for chat. Baseline goals: p95 latency <= 120ms for chat (single-turn), throughput target 180–220 concurrent inference QPS sustained during peak claim surges, burstable to 400 QPS for up to 15 minutes.

Key technical asks observed in evaluation:
- Throughput guarantees: want committed GPU pool that can sustain 200 QPS with <150ms median gen latency for the curated model family. Expect Redwood to provide sizing guidance (gpus, nvlink, memory per shard) and a migration plan.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets and measurable token-level breakdown. Customer insists on p95 <120ms for chat, p99 <350ms for heavy extraction flows.
- Reserved GPU planning: preference to reserve 8 x A100-class GPUs (or equivalent) across 2 AZs with local warm pools to reduce cold-starts. Will consider fractional shard sizing if cost-optimal.
- SLA negotiations: target 99.95% uptime for inference control plane, 4-hour response for Sev1, and financial credits on breach. Also need clear RTO/RPO for KV cache warming after node replacement.
- Autoscaling / capacity management specifics (primary topic):
  * Scale-up policy: reactive + predictive hybrid. React within 30–60s for sustained spike >20% baseline; predictive warm-up for scheduled batch windows (08:00–11:00 local) using historical load curve.
  * Warm pools: require 2 warm GPU instances per shard (hot standby) to keep k-v cache primed for low-latency reroutes. Warm pools must be warm enough to serve <100ms token gen overhead.
  * Scale-down policy: conservative cooldown (10–20 minutes) + gradual decommission to avoid oscillation; preserve last-used KV caches for priority customers for 30 minutes before eviction.
  * Queueing behavior: bounded queue with backpressure for non-critical background batch jobs, priority lanes for premium customers and realtime adjuster chat. Want SLA-aware queuing (timeouts, early rejection thresholds).
  * Cost controls: soft caps and token-based throttles per account tier; ability to shift lower-priority traffic to cheaper quantized model variants automatically during capacity contention.

Security & compliance notes: CISO flagged KMS integration and audit trail granularity. Need proof of HSM-encrypted key management and per-request audit IDs. Data residency: claims PII must remain in US regions.

Procurement/legal: Received draft SOW and SLA; legal sent redlines focusing on uptime credits, incident notification windows, and data deletion certification for deprovisioning.

Open items (actionable):
- Redwood to provide concrete Dedicated sizing recommendation (gpu type/count, network topology) and cost delta vs. Hosted fallback (due 2026-02-17).
- Deliver an autoscaling runbook: exact scale-up thresholds, warm-pool management, queue sizing, and test plan for failover drills (due 2026-02-24).
- SE to attach POC perf artifacts: token-level latencies, heatmaps, and resource utilization (attached to Drive).

Quotes/voice notes: "We need predictable capacity during invoice cycles — can't afford jitter when 10k claims hit the system in an hour." — Head of Platform

Next tactical: schedule procurement + security deep-dive (Redwood SOC2 evidence + KMS integration call) and finalize reserved GPU proposal.
